agenda.2026-11-30-allemagne-inflation-no: Germany: first estimate of November inflation

Germany's statistics office Destatis publishes its provisional estimate of November prices on Monday 30 November at 2 p.m. [1]. In October, inflation had eased to 2.8% year on year, after 3.3% in September [2]: together with France and Spain, this figure sets the trend for the euro area ahead of the ECB meeting on 17 December.
agenda.2026-12-23-belgique-inflation-dec: Belgium: December inflation and wage indexation

Statbel publishes the December price index on 23 December; a new indexation of wages and benefits is expected this month [1]. In November, Belgian inflation stayed above 5% (5.09%), driven by energy (+33.7% year on year) [2]: it weighs on companies' labour costs.
Date of 23 December and expected indexation given by loonindex.be; Statbel's official calendar could not be checked.
agenda.2027-02-28-vietnam-enquete-301.ti: Washington must rule on its trade investigation into Vietnam (intellectual property)
agenda.2027-02-28-vietnam-enquete-301.wh: The United States has pushed back by three months, to 28 February 2027, its decision in the "Section 301" investigation into intellectual property in Vietnam [1][2]. Vietnam is already targeted by another procedure, announced on 25 November, which proposes up to 35% in additional tariffs [3]: the threat to its exports to the United States is growing.
agenda.2026-11-29-opep-reunion-semestrie: OPEC+ meets on Sunday 29 November to set its 2027 production quotas [1][2]: without a deal, the group has no production framework after 31 December [2]. With prices falling on fears of oversupply, delegates are talking about a simple one-month extension of the current ceilings [2]; the decision will set the tone for oil prices this winter.
agenda.2026-12-01-zone-euro-inflation-no: Euro area: first estimate of November inflation

Eurostat publishes its flash estimate of November price growth on 1 December [1][2]. In October, inflation had reached 4.0%, its highest level in three years [3]; the first national figures point to a slowdown, to 2.9% in France [4] and 4.1% in Spain [5], thanks to fuel. It is the last major figure before the ECB meeting on 17 December.
agenda.2026-12-06-israel-delai-eisenkot-: Israel: end of the initial 28-day period given to Gadi Eisenkot to form a government

Tasked on 8 November with forming a coalition, Eisenkot has 28 days, which can be extended by 14 [1]. He has signed a deal with Yair Golan's Democrats [2][3] but accuses Netanyahu's Likud of dragging out the talks [4]: without a majority, Israel would remain without a new government in the middle of the war with Iran.
